title: The Resistance Is Here
gist: Scientists who never intended to be activists have united to fight the Trump administration's drastic cuts to science, exemplified by an Emory addiction researcher told to strip banned words and demographic references from her federal grant application.

insights.claim: Scientists who did not plan to become activists have united in an effort to overturn the Trump administration's drastic cuts to science.
insights.speaker: Adam Piore
insights.so_what: Signals an organized political mobilization within the research community—an emerging force in science-policy fights.
insights.locator: scientists have united to overturn Trump’s drastic cuts to science

insights.claim: Colette Delawalla, a 30-year-old Emory University addiction researcher, was told that to keep her federal grant she would have to remove the words 'marijuana' and 'opioids' and all references to gender, race, and sexual orientation.
insights.speaker: Adam Piore
insights.so_what: A concrete example of content-based conditions being imposed on federal research funding.
insights.locator: she’d need to revise her application and remove the words

insights.claim: The demanded revisions were an impossible ask for an addiction scientist whose dissertation on alcohol-use disorder relied on a dataset chosen to reflect the demographic diversity of the 2020 census.
insights.speaker: Adam Piore
insights.so_what: Illustrates how the funding conditions directly conflict with scientific methodology.
insights.locator: It was an impossible ask for an addiction scientist
